assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell is a genuine new concept of molecular organisation: membraneless compartments governed by multivalency, thermodynamic phase behaviour and interfacial physics. It reduces a messy cell-biological phenomenon to general physical-chemical principles, and has reshaped thinking in cell biology, neurodegeneration (including aggregation and amyloid-like transitions) and soft matter.
assessment.attribution: The 2009 P-granule work of Brangwynne and Hyman is the founding demonstration; Rosen and colleagues supplied the multivalent-interaction, phase-transition framework in 2012. Pappu and Mittag contributed sequence-encoded physical theory and biophysics that are also important. Three people (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen) is the cleanest configuration but it excludes valuable physical-chemistry contributors.
assessment.maturity: Roughly 15 years of rapid, broad confirmation across many systems. Impact is wide, but the field is still maturing and the timing is reasonable rather than clearly late.
uncertainties: Debate on which cellular condensates are true equilibrium phase separation versus other assemblies, and on in vivo functional relevance.
Allocation of credit between the cell-biology discovery and the physical-chemical framework is unresolved.
I am recalling the history from memory and have not verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are lipid self-assembly put to work: control of lipid phase behaviour, pKa-dependent charge and membrane fusion enable systemic nucleic-acid delivery. The outcome is enormous (siRNA drug Onpattro, mRNA vaccines), and the underlying lipid physical chemistry is the part I know best and consider decisive.
assessment.attribution: The Cullis group at UBC (with Madden and Hope) developed the lipid-nanoparticle formulation and the ionizable-lipid approach; Langer, Anderson and industrial teams contributed delivery chemistry and later lipid optimisation. A three-person UBC configuration is defensible but others (Anderson, Langer, MacLachlan) have a real claim and the allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Decades of development, clinical approval, and global deployment give very strong maturity. Recognition is timely, with the 2023 Medicine prize having honoured the nucleoside-modification half of the story.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior Medicine recognition of mRNA vaccines might make a Chemistry award read as a second prize for the same story.
Credit is distributed across academia and industry with patent-related disputes.
Details recalled from memory and unverified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation via PROTACs and molecular glues introduced a new pharmacological modality in which small molecules induce proximity and hijack ubiquitin ligases. Conceptually original and with growing clinical translation, it is rooted in the chemistry of induced protein-protein interfaces and ternary-complex thermodynamics.
assessment.attribution: Crews (with Deshaies and Sakamoto) invented PROTACs; Ciulli's VHL ligands and structural work made them drug-like; Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, explaining molecular glues. Eight credited names is too many; the three chosen cover the modality, the enabling chemistry and the molecular-glue mechanism, though it omits Deshaies and Gray.
assessment.maturity: Clinical trials are advanced and many degraders are in the clinic, but no approved PROTAC yet as far as I know. Possibly slightly early for the full impact.
uncertainties: Lack of approved degrader drugs and long-term clinical impact.
Fair division of credit among PROTAC inventors versus molecular-glue mechanism discoverers is unresolved.
Clinical status recalled from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another without double-strand breaks through engineered deaminase chemistry on DNA. It is original, creative molecular design with immediate therapeutic reach and broad use in research.
assessment.attribution: Liu's lab is the clear originator of both cytosine and adenine base editors; Komor and Gaudelli were the lead researchers on the key papers. A single laureate is the cleanest configuration, and pairing with the CRISPR laureates avoids too much overlap in this field.
assessment.maturity: Clinical use is emerging, with first patients treated, and independent confirmation is extensive. Timing is reasonable though not overdue.
uncertainties: Relationship to the 2020 CRISPR-Cas9 prize may reduce perceived novelty.
Whether prime editing (a separate candidate) should be recognised together with base editing is open.
Clinical outcomes still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry of intact protein complexes lets one measure stoichiometry, interactions, lipid binding and membrane protein assemblies in the gas phase, preserving non-covalent organisation. It is a physical-chemical method with much relevance for membrane-protein and lipid-protein interactions.
assessment.attribution: Robinson pioneered native MS of large complexes and membrane proteins, Heck extended it to broad complexes and proteomics, and Chait contributed early non-covalent MS and structural applications. Loo and Gross also have claims, so the choice is open to debate.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent adoption and wide use make this a mature technology, though a Chemistry prize for MS has recently occurred (2002), which may dilute the case.
uncertainties: Overlap with candidates on proteomics MS (B012) and the precedent of the 2002 MS prize.
Whether gas-phase structures faithfully reflect solution structures remains debated.
Credit boundaries are unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory with the principle of minimal frustration reduced protein folding to statistical-mechanical physical chemistry, and explained how sequences find unique structures. Together with experimental mapping of folding pathways, it is an elegant general concept.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes, Onuchic and Bryngelson developed the funnel and landscape theory; Fersht established the experimental phi-value approach. Dill's hydrophobic-collapse ideas are a further contribution. A theory-plus-experiment trio is workable but contested.
assessment.maturity: Concepts have been consolidated for 30 years, though the 2024 prize to protein structure prediction and design may alter perception of the folding problem.
uncertainties: Debate over how much landscape theory has directly enabled predictive progress.
Overlap with the AlphaFold prize of 2024 and recognition of folding versus structure prediction.
Allocation of credit among theorists is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers and soft lithography established molecular control of surfaces and interfaces, with strong thermodynamic and colloid-chemistry roots, and built tools used across chemistry, biology and engineering. A classic concept of spontaneous molecular organisation at interfaces.
assessment.attribution: Nuzzo and Allara demonstrated alkanethiol monolayers on gold, with Whitesides providing the broad development and soft lithography; Sagiv's earlier silane monolayers complicate priority. A three-person prize is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of confirmation, and arguably overdue, though some of the conceptual novelty is now diffuse and part of the surface-science tradition.
uncertainties: Priority issue with Sagiv and excluded contributors such as Xia.
Whether the Academy sees this as a single discovery or a collection of techniques.
Details unverified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-directed self-assembly of discrete cages and capsules is a clear case of the programmed assembly of complex architectures from simple parts through thermodynamic control, with uses in encapsulation, confined reactivity and sensing. It is physically intuitive and conceptually original.
assessment.attribution: Fujita, Raymond and Stang each independently established distinct design principles (Pd-based cages, M-L assemblies and tetrahedra, and supramolecular coordination complexes), providing a natural trio. Nitschke and Ward are later extenders.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of confirmation; recognition is arguably timely given the 2025 prize for metal-organic frameworks, but that may also overlap and make this less likely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 MOF prize and with earlier supramolecular prizes (1987, 2016).
Practical impact is less broad than other candidates.
Facts recalled from memory.
